children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's lovely to meet you, and I'm happy to help you work out if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

I have a few more questions to understand your situation:

Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me. He lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex lives with his mum rather than with you, I need to understand a bit more about the situation.

Are you contributing towards Alex's upkeep? For example, do you pay maintenance or contribute financially towards his care in some way?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do contribute towards his upkeep. I help out with money for his clothes, school things, and other expenses he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I understand you contribute towards Alex's upkeep even though he lives with his mum.

I have a couple more questions to help determine your eligibility:

1. Is Alex's mum currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, she is claiming Child Benefit for him already.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is an important detail.

Under Child Benefit rules, **only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any one time**. Since Alex's mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you would not be able to make a separate claim for him.

If you wanted to receive Child Benefit for Alex instead of his mum, one of you would need to contact the Child Benefit Office to change who receives the payment. His mum would need to stop her claim, and then you could make a new claim. However, this would require agreement between you both.

Generally, when a child lives with one parent and the other parent contributes financially, the parent the child lives with is usually the one who claims Child Benefit.

Would you like me to confirm this as my final eligibility assessment for Alex, or do you have any other questions?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I understand. So just to be clear - because his mum is already claiming it and Alex lives with her, I'm not eligible to claim Child Benefit for him right now, is that right?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, that's exactly right. Since Alex lives with his mum and she is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

The key rules are:
- Only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child
- When a child lives with someone else who is already claiming, that claim takes priority

Your financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep are valuable for his care, but they don't override the existing claim made by the person he lives with.

If your circumstances were to change in the future (for example, if Alex came to live with you, or if his mum decided to stop her claim), you could then make a claim yourself.

Let me provide you with my formal eligibility assessment now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
To summarise my assessment:

**Child Benefit Eligibility for Alex: Not Eligible**

**Reason:** Alex lives with his mum, who is already claiming Child Benefit for him. Since only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child at any one time, and his mum has an existing claim as the resident parent, you are not currently eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

If your circumstances change in the future — for example, if Alex comes to live with you, or if his mum agrees to stop her claim so you can claim instead — you would then be able to apply.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
